text:
Brock Nelson passed 1,000 NHL games last season, and early in his second full season with the Avalanche the scoring has gone quiet. He has 10 points in 18 games and just 3 in his last ten, and his ice time has dropped by about two minutes a night to under 17.

This is not mostly bad luck. His team's finishing with him on the ice is right at expected, and his own 4 goals sit just under 4.9 expected goals. His chance rate has dipped to 0.94 expected goals per 60, from 1.10 last season. At five on five Colorado still takes about 56% of the expected goals with him out there, so his line is not losing its minutes.

He also took a shot to the ear against Calgary, per Yahoo Sports, after scoring in that game, and was back for the next one. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 98th percentile among forwards for driving play. At 35, the question is whether the chance rate comes back. We'd watch his shots and his minutes before his points.
headline: Nelson's scoring has stalled in Colorado
